# Batch Processing - File Reconciliation - PowerCARD-Solution


## 1 Introduction


## 1.1 Document objective

This document is an operational guide of PowerCARD solution. It is useful to understand the processes implemented within the solution to allow the customer to define their internal operational procedures.


## 1.2 Operating context of the solution

Skills required for managing PowerCARD solutions from operating point of view are Oracle DBA and a system engineer (AIX and Websphere ).


Common administration tasks are:
- 1. Evaluate the database and application server hardware
- 2. PowerCARD Application and database backup
- 3. Monitoring data volume,
- 4. User management,
- 5. Batch organization and monitoring.



## 1.3 Operations principles

The figure bellow depicts the main technical actors handling PowerCARD operational environment:

Figure 1: Operation Administration and Management


In general, the operation administration and management covers the activities:
- 1. Technical operations,
- 2. Technical monitoring,
- 3. Business supervision,

- 4. Reporting and analysis.



Hereafter the definitions of main flows identified in the application and which are helpful to understand the next sections of the document:
- 1. Return code of a batch to indicate if the process ended successfully or unsuccessfully. This information is communicated to the batch scheduler (ex.: Dollar Universe, Control M…),
- 2. Return flow as a response to a processing flow : it is communicated to the third system which has initially initiate the process, to advise it about what has been performed (ex. : CFT acknowledgment, return file …),
- 3. Event report « CRE » or activity report: It is a file used for reporting and analysis further to the extraction of data from the database,
- 4. Processing report: information stored in log files communicated to the supervision agent like PATROL.



Four levels are identified to manage the day to day operations and the incidents:
- ·


Level 1 : technical operations,


- · Level 2 : system infrastructure administration, software's, production network,
- · Level 3 : technical-functional support of PowerCARD application,
- · Level 4 : HPS support.

## 2 Batches processing


In this section, we describe:
- 1. The definition and architecture of a PowerCARD batch
- 2. The diagram syntax of a PowerCARD batch
- 3. Architecture batches
- 4. Running a batch
- 5. Encryption


Batches will be designed by (batch_name) within this section.


## 2.1 Definitions

A PowerCARD batch is a set of processes that is using the data available in the database to perform functional processes, generate files or load files.

A chain refers to running a group of these kinds of batches.


## 2.2 Diagram Syntax

Figure 2: Batch "figures syntax"


## 2.3 Architecture

In 3 tiers architecture, batch components are shared between application tier and database tier. PowerCARD batches (standard & ETL) follow the same rules for setting inputs parameters and outputs trace file.

Figure 3: Architecture Components

# Batch Processing - File Reconciliation - PowerCARD-Solution


## 2.3.1 Components of the application tier


## 2.3.1.1 Shell


It is the starting point of a process. Two parameters are communicated to the shell:
- · Names of the binary,
- · Log file to use.



## 2.3.1.2 Binary file


It is the key driver of the batch:
- · Get the parameters defined at the task level
- · Load, if needed, the input file(s) using the control files
- · Call the PL/SQL functional process
- · Generate output files
- · Store the summary of the process in its own log file
- · Send back the execution error code [1: OK, 11: Warning and 99: Error].



## 2.3.1.3 Ctl file


The SQL*Loader control file is a text file that contains data definition language [DDL] instructions. The DDL is used to control:
- · Where SQL*Loader will find the data to load
- · How SQL*Loader expects that data to be formatted
- · How SQL*Loader will be configured (memory management, rejecting records, interrupted load handling, and so on) as it loads the data
- · How SQL*Loader will manipulate the data being loaded



## Confidential

# Batch Processing - File Reconciliation - PowerCARD-Solution

Control file will be present only for batches which need to load data from file into the database.

The processing is performed on two steps. The first one is loading the content of the file in a temporary table(s). The second one refers to the functional process where the data is extracted from temporary table(s), processed and stored in the destination tables. If an error occurs in the first step the temporary table(s) are purged and the process need to be performed form the beginning (total rollback).


## Note

This file is only created when the process updates tables based on the input of a file.


## 2.3.1.4 Grf file

It refers to the configuration graphs files used by the ETL module. The graphs files are called directly from the shell once the ETL is launched.


## 2.3.2 Component of the database tiers


## 2.3.2.1 Task in Pcard_Tasks

A task or a batch is defined in PCARD_TASKS table and a new task can be parametrized in this table.

Generally, there is one entry per task in PCARD_TASKS table. This entry contains the processing date and the parameters required by the binary file. The task has usually the same name as the binary with some exceptions.

To handle performance issues for batches that deal with large amount of data, a parallel execution concept is used by PowerCARD. The parallel process uses two parameters tables PCARD_TASKS_JOBS and PCARD_TASKS_JOB_PARAM to set the number of simultaneous jobs and other required parametrizations.


## 2.3.2.2 Packages related to a task process

The functional process of a task is contained in PLS/SQL packages. Once the parameters are communicated to the main package and eventually data is loaded in temporary tables, the functional process may start.

Error messages are logged in PCARD_TRACES and PCARD_ERRORS, while the processing status, OK or KO, is transmitted to the binary file to be written in its trace file.


## 2.4 Running a batch


In the application tier, we are using environment variables to access rapidly to the working directories:
- · $BIN : directory for binary files
- · $SHL : directory containing shell scripts
- · $CTL : directory for SQL*Loader control files
- · $TRACE : directory which contains Trace files
- · $DATA : directory where received and generated files are stored. Note that we can manage storing files under sub directories of $DATA directory.
- · $ARCHIVE : directory where files are moved to


To start a batch, 2 steps are required:

# Batch Processing - File Reconciliation - PowerCARD-Solution


- 1. Set in the database the batch parameters
- 2. Launch the shell file from the application tier



## 2.4.1 Defining the batch parameters


The parameters of a batch (task) are defined in PCARD_TASKS table; they need to be filled or updated each time the batch is run:
- · STATUS: To be set to P (Pending)
- · BUSINESS_DATE: Date of the processing.
- · PARAMETER_V1_DATA: 1st parameter of the task (depends on the task)
- · …
- · PARAMETER_V10_DATA: 10th parameter of the task (can be null it depends on the task).


Screen path: Administration > Jobs > Jobs parameters

Figure 4: Jobs parameters (Details screen)

Figure 5: Jobs parameters (Parameters tab)

If the batch is executed from the screen, the user is required to capture the batch parameters, and the update of the database is done automatically.

The screen above is defined during the initial deployment of PowerCARD, and it is not recommended to modify theses settings. Since theses settings will only affect the launching screen and not the batch itself, if a parameter is set to not be mandatory, this parameter remains mandatory while the screen would not display it, and eventually create incoherences.

If the batch is executed by a script used to automate the batch scheduling, the following script $BIN/update_pcard_tasks is required to update the Bank Code, task parameters, task status and the business date.

# Batch Processing - File Reconciliation - PowerCARD-Solution


## Syntax to call the "update_pcard_tasks" binary file:


- $ $BIN/update_pcard_tasks update_pcard_tasks <log file update_pcard_tasks> <task_name> <bank_code 123456 <business_date_DDMMYYYY> <PAR_1> <PAR_2> <PAR_3> <PAR_4> <PAR_5> <PAR_6> <PAR_7> <PAR_8> <PAR_9> <PAR_10>



## Where:


- · Bank_code: The institution ID number to have this task executed. This field is mandatory.. Several banks can be included separated by commas.
- · Task_name: Name of the task to be executed.
- · Business_date_DDMMYYYY: business date to communicate to the batch. It has to have BDDMMYYYY format, or '' to use the current business date of the system.
- · PAR_X: Value of the X parameter or Null. 256 characters maximum.


The batch returns 1 (OK) or 99 (KO) and does not generate neither a log file nor an error code. It is not considered as PowerCARD batch.

Return code listing: 00004, 00019, 00021, 99999.


## 2.4.2 Most common parameters examples and values


PowerCARD provide maximum flexibly in the scheduling of the batch by reusing the same set of parameters for several batches. Here is a short listing of the most common parameters with their possible values, or since the parameters are configuration based how to obtain them:
- · Origin code: Origin code value is to design the source and type of the transaction. Possible values are:



| Source description                     | Type    |   Possible values |
|----------------------------------------|---------|-------------------|
| ON US CARD / LOCAL MERCHANT            | CHAR(1) |                 0 |
| ON US CARD / LOCAL OTHER BANK MERCHANT | CHAR(1) |                 1 |
| ON US CARD / FOREIGN MERCHANT          | CHAR(1) |                 2 |
| LOCAL OTHER BANK CARD / LOCAL MERCHANT | CHAR(1) |                 3 |
| FOREIGN CARD / LOCAL MERCHANT          | CHAR(1) |                 4 |



- · Network code: This is used to identify the network either as a source or destination of the transactions. These are the typical values:



| Source description   | Type    |   Possible values |
|----------------------|---------|-------------------|
| VISA                 | CHAR(2) |                01 |
| MASTERCARD           | CHAR(2) |                02 |
| EUROPAY              | CHAR(2) |                03 |
| AMEX                 | CHAR(2) |                04 |
| DINERS               | CHAR(2) |                05 |
| JCB                  | CHAR(2) |                06 |
| DISCOVER             | CHAR(2) |                07 |

# Batch Processing - File Reconciliation - PowerCARD-Solution


## Note

Other values may be added for private network


- · Bank code: Bank ID: This is the identity code of Institutions managed by the PowerCARD platform. As this information varies per customers, it is not provided in this document. However, a PowerCARD user may get the listing via Parameters > Institution > Institution or via a database query : ' select bank_code, center_code, bank_name from BANK; '.



Furthermore, this parameter can be used in the following fashion:
- · Specific bank code: "123456" the batch will be executed for this specific Bank ID
- · For all Banks
- · Non reporting Batch: the parameter 'ALL' must be specified to process data for all Institutions defined in Platform
- · Reporting batch the parameter is null to generate reports or data files for all Institutions defined in Platform
- · For a discrete number of Banks: separated by commas: "123456, 234567" this mode of operation only works for reports i.e. Reporting Section.
- · Reason code: This is listing of reason code for transactions.


Possible values are:

NON PAYMENT OF FEES, SIGNATURE DIFFERS, Reverse TC - without fee etc. As these values vary per customer, a full listing is not provided. However, a PowerCARD analyst may access the full listing via the screen : Parameters > Platform > Transaction codes or via a database query : ' select bank_code, reason_code, reason_code_wording from TRANS_REASON_CODE; '


- · Card product: Describe the type of product (VISA DEBIT,MC Platinum Credit Card, MC Gold, etc.). As this is specific per customer, it is not described in this document. However, an analyst with access to PowerCARD can obtain a listing via the screens PARAMETER>GENERAL>CARDHOLDER:PRODUCT CODE or using database access via the query : ' select bank_code, product_code, wording from CARD_PRODUCT; '
- · Transaction definition: Describe the type of transaction. As this is specific per customer, they are not specified in this document. However, a full listing may be obtained either via the PowerCARD screen : PARAMETER>ISSUING>REVOLVING CREDIT:TRANSACTIONS:TRANSACTION REASON or via a database query: ' select transaction_code, wording from TRANSACTION_DEFINITION; '
- · Account profile code: This is used to describe the type of the account (debit, pre-paid, credit, etc.). As this is specific per customer, these are not detailed in this document. However, an PowerCARD analyst may obtain them via PARAMETER>ISSUING> REVOLVING CREDIT>PROFILE:CREDIT PROFILE DEFINITION: or via a database query: ' select bank_code, profile_code , wording from CR_PROFILE;'
- · Language: User language is selected via the screen at the login stage or specified via parameter during command line execution. The most common values are en_EN for English, es_ES for Spanish and fr_FR for French.
- · Account status: Administrative status of the account (Normal, Collection, etc). These are specific per customer and are not detailed in this document; however, here is how to obtain the full listing via PowerCARD PARAMETER>ISSUING>REVOLVING CREDIT:CREDIT ACCOUNT STATUSor via a database query : ' select profile_code,wording from SHADOW_ACCOUNT_STATUS; '

## 2.4.3 Update of the business date

If the business date is left to NULL, the current business set in PowerCARD will be used.

The choice to pass the business date is left up to the operational team; however it is a best practice to systematically include the business date as part of the update of the script to avoid errors.

The actual value of the business date is an operational decision or based upon business requirement.


## 2.4.4 Execute a shell

From the application tier, the shell file is executed and the trace file name to use is mentioned. The name of the trace file padded by 000, and this number is incremented by 1 each time the process cannot write in the log file.

Example: load_posting_new_file.sh load_posting_new_file.trc000 POSTFLIN will generate a trace file load_posting_new_file.trc000 and if the trace file reached the maximum size "1024" bytes, the shell will increment the sequence and generate load_posting_new_file.trc001 file.

## 2.4.5.7 Output data

Generally the output files are generated under $DATA directory

## 2.4.5.8 Counters

It contains the description of the counters that will be written in the batch log file. It is an extraction of the text part only of the log file, the prefix part plus timestamp and PIDs are removed.


These counters have to be analyzed in day to day operations. Classic counters are:
- · Processed (Total number of records)
- · Succeed (number of records successfully processed)
- · Rejected (number of records unsuccessfully processed)


A record can be an authorization, a transaction…


## 2.4.5.9 Warning

This paragraph aims to describe if a process can end with Warning. The batches can end with Warning when a subset of records cannot be processed for technical reasons and not functional ones. Some batches have a threshold parametrized in the table REMITTANCE_AGENT so that the batch will end with ERROR if it's met. The other batches keep WARNING status.

Relevant SQL queries will be provided as well as the relevant error codes for the specific batch.

This chapter has to be used when there is an error during the execution of a batch and once the origin of the error is identified and corrected.

It explains the recovery procedure mode, the parameters to set to re-start the batch and if the batch will start the processing from the beginning or from the crash point. It is mentioned also if the chain has to be stopped and the database needs to be cleaned before restarting the batch.

|            | · Not available - no recovery ·                                                                             |
|            | From the beginning - The process restart from the beginning                                                 |

## 2.4.6 Batch multi-cutoff support

Multi-cutoff support has been introduced for some batches for the PowerCARD V3.5.

This functionality allows processor or large institution to run concurrent jobs in parallel for a pre-configured group of institutions.

## 2.5 Native file encryption

PowerCARD comes with native file encryption to comply with PCI requirements.

Implementation of the encryption is achieved via openSSL libraries deployed during the initial setup of PowerCARD at the customer's premises. Customer must pay special attention to the choice of passphrase and its management. It is strongly recommended that this passphrase be managed as per Pin Security and Management procedures.


## Note

No recovery of lost passphrase is possible. Please ensure dual control of passphrase are in place.


The exact type of encryption used is defined during the implementation yet these 4 elements will be produced:
- · Public key: Used to encrypt all of the data. This file can be shared without issue. It must remain on the server to be able to encrypt new files.
- · Private key (in clear): Used to decrypt the data. This file must be protected by a strong passphrase. The private key must not be stored on the server in clear. A copy should be kept in cold storage as part of the disaster recovery plan.
- · Private key (encrypted): This file contains the secured version of the clear private key, and must be kept on the server to allow decryption.
- · Strong passphrase: This is a more complex version of a password used to secure the clear private key. It will be required for every decryption files.


To decipher any files, the following command must be used :


```
openssl smime -decrypt  -in   <encrypted filename> file  -binary -inform DEM inkey $HOME/usr/cfg/rsa/ pwc_privatekey.pem     -out   <Clear filename> .
```

The user will then be prompted for the passphrase and the resulting clear filename be created in the $data directory.

## Note


- · PowerCARD encrypts all the interfaces files exchange
- · Report generated by PowerCARD must not be encrypted. As such a control file ensures that only the reports are kept in clear text.


The control file is located in: $/SHL/encrypt_file.prm


PCI considerations: the control file must be audited regularly and have the proper permission set to the right users:
- · System administrator : full control and ownership
- · PowerCARD users (including batch users) : read only rights
- · Other users: no access
- · No execution privilege for anyone.

## SQL * Loader traces

## PCARD_TASKS Table

This is the table that contains all batches processing, their parameters and storing their execution status.


## Content


Main columns of the table are as follows:
- · TASK_NAME: It has the same name of the job
- · STATUS: The batch status ('S'uccessful, 'U'nsuccessful ou 'P'ending)
- · ENDING_STATUS: Return code of the last execution.
- · BUSINESS_DATE : The processing date used for the job execution
- · PARAMETER_VX_DATA : Values of the parameters X used for the job execution
- · COUNTER_X : Values of the counters X linked to the last job execution
- · AMOUNT_X : Values of the amounts X linked to the last job execution



## PCARD_TRACES Table

This table contains all errors or information messages generated during the job execution.


## Content


Below themaintable columns:
- · TASK_ID : batch identifier (it is shown on thetrace file of thebatch)
- · PACKAGE_NAME and FUNCTION_NAME : PL-SQL Package and Function that generate the error
- · USER_MESSAGE : Detail of the error
- · ORA_ERROR_CODE : Oracle Error Code
- · ERROR_CODE: Error code in PowerCARD format PWC-00000.



## PCARD_MESSAGE_APP Table

It is the repository table of PowerCARD batches error codes batches PowerCARD .

- · APP_CODE : Application Module
- · ERROR_CODE : Error code in PowerCARD format PWC-00000
- · ERROR_NAME : Name of the Error code
- · MESSAGE : Detail of the error

## 2.6.3 GUI (Graphical User Interface) logs and traces

The application traces of PowerCARD (and stack traces) are logged in the global JVM file of the WebSphere server 'SystemOut.log'.

The messages are following the (was7) format

[1/7/13 15:02:51:711 CST] 0000002f MessageBroker I org.springframework.flex.servlet.MessageBrokerHandlerAdapter handle Channel endpoint my-secure-amf received request.


Each line is interpreted as follows:
- · timestamp


In the example, the timestamp is [1/7/13 15:02:51:711 CST].

The format of the timestamp is based on the location setup of the process server. It includes a complete date with millisecond precision and a time zone.


- · Thread Identifier


In the example the thread ID is 0000002f. The thread ID is a hexadecimal code of 8 positions generated from the hash code of the thread that generates the message.


- · Class

In the example the class is MessageBroker.

The class is the abbreviated name of the component that generates the message. For WAS, it will be the class of the component that generates the message, and for applications (PWC) the class of the object used to generate the message.


- · Event Type



In the example the event type is I. The event type is a 1 character. Possible values are:
- · F Fatal Error

- · A Audit message

- · O standard output console (System.out) of an application or an internal component of WAS
